Audi Concept Q Virtually Reinterprets the Original Audi Quattro for the New Age of Electrification
20 photos
Photo: angelodilor_design / Instagram
The Ingolstadt-based automaker hasn’t been feeling all too well over the past couple of years, with dwindling sales across the globe and massive drops in places that count more than others in the grand scheme of things – like North America.
Hopefully, things are going to change going into 2027, as the company has just about anything for everyone across the board, from the recently relaunched Audi A2, which came back to life just as quirky but as an e-tron model, right up to the new hero supercar , the Audi Nuvolari.
More importantly, there is also cool stuff in between them for the North American market, such as the all-new Audi A6 Allroad, which is a worthy mid-size station wagon alternative to crossover SUVs, while the brand also doesn’t neglect the latter thanks to the newly introduced third-generation Audi Q7 and its first-ever Audi Q9 sibling with three rows of seats and flagship credentials worthy of a clash with the likes of the Cadillac Escalade and especially the BMW X7 and Mercedes-Benz GLS.
As such, it’s no wonder that everyone – including the rumor mill and the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI- is keeping an eye on them. For example, just recently, Angelo Di Lorenzi, a former Exterior Design intern at Alfa Romeo and now a Junior Exterior Designer known as ' angelodilor_design ' on social media, envisioned the potential new-age return of the iconic Audi Quattro road and rally car.
It’s not a typo – Audi decided to rename its quattro four-wheel-drive system with all small letters in honor of the Audi Quattro, which launched at the 1980 Geneva Motor Show, almost three decades ago, as a model that sought to take advantage of the new rally rules of the era that finally allowed the use of four-wheel drive in competition racing. Dubbed the Audi Ur-Quattro, aka the primordial quattro model, the two-door coupe remains an important part of Audi’s modern legacy.
It also helped that it had a particular design, with the model related but not akin to the B2 Audi 80 compact executive sedan. Anyway, now the pixel master wants to show us their “personal vision of the next chapter in the Audi Quattro story, exploring how its distinctive proportions, strong character, and rally heritage could be reinterpreted through a design approach that balances the original’s bold identity with a more contemporary aesthetic.”
This means that the CGI expert keeps the defining signature traits of the original Audi Quattro, like the fastback shape and the square headlight style, along with the full-width black treatment of the taillights, which were actually connected by a styling element, not fully lit. But, of course, now it’s all mixed with contemporary widebody attire and slim LED elements, both at the front and around the back.
